summary: A one-screen utility page for a pictogram font of macOS system cursors: a one-sentence description with a Download button, then a plain 5-column keymap grid of the 41 cursor glyphs, each cell labelled with the key that types it and (on mobile, or on hover) the matching CSS cursor value; a glyph follower replaces the pointer with the font's own cursor.

instances.look: No hero: one paragraph across the top in a large system-like serif/sans mix ('Cursor.otf beta is a font by Liebermann Kiepe Reddemann that allows you to use the MacOS system cursors as a font…') ending in a grey rounded 'Download' pill
instances.feel: Dry, tool-like, in on the joke
instances.ux: Studio name links to the studio; the pill downloads the OTF
instances.learn: For a utility font, a single explanatory sentence can replace hero, story and CTA at once

reconstruction.layout: Full-width text block at the top-left, ~1420px wide, 3 lines (~150px), 10px padding; the grid starts directly beneath
reconstruction.typography: ~32px 'TimesNewArial' (the studio's own Times/Arial hybrid with ital and srff axes), black, leading ~1.1; button label same size in a light grey pill
reconstruction.content: One factual sentence describing the font and its use (implying interaction in website sketches)

instances.look: An inline grey pill 'Download' at the end of the intro sentence
instances.ux: Direct link to the .otf file, no licence text or form
instances.learn: Put the download button inline at the end of the only sentence: the CTA is part of the description

reconstruction.layout: Inline button after the last word, ~110×34px, radius ~17px
reconstruction.typography: Same ~32px sans as the sentence, black on light grey

instances.look: A 5-column grid of light grey cells separated by 1px black rules; each cell has its key (0–5, R, B, K, N, X, m, +, -, ?, C, c, t, T, r, d, x, s, y, a, q, w, e, h, v, E, Q, H, V, W, S, M, A, D, p) in small type top-left and the cursor glyph (grab hand, arrow, spinning wait, copy-plus, not-allowed, zoom, I-beam, resize arrows, crosshair) centred
instances.ux: On desktop a follower element replaces the pointer with the font's own cursor glyph for the hovered key; the matching CSS value ('cursor: grabbing', 'cursor: nesw-resize') is in each cell, visible under the glyph on mobile
instances.learn: For a pictogram font, label every cell with the key to type and the real-world name (here the CSS cursor value): it becomes a cheat sheet for DTP users and web developers alike

reconstruction.layout: Full-width CSS grid, 5 columns × 288px, rows ~176px, 1px black borders, 41 cells over ~1.75 screens; on mobile 2 columns with taller cells
reconstruction.typography: Key labels ~13px sans top-left; cursor glyphs 36px in the Cursor font, centred; CSS value ~13px sans bottom-left
reconstruction.behaviour: Mouse move drives a fixed .follower holding a .letter in the Cursor font that tracks the pointer and shows the hovered cell's key (jQuery script.js); grid otherwise static
reconstruction.content: All 41 cursor glyphs mapped to keys, with CSS cursor equivalents (default, pointer, grab, grabbing, wait, progress, copy, no-drop, not-allowed, context-menu, zoom-in, zoom-out, help, cell, crosshair, text, vertical-text, alias, *-resize, move, all-scroll)
reconstruction.assets: none (the glyphs come from the font; colour cursors like the wait spinner and copy badge are colour glyphs)
